sentences.text: Pre-operative multi-sequence MRI: axial T1, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce), T2 and FLAIR, co-registered, skull-stripped and resampled to 1 mm isotropic (BraTS preparation).
The tumour contains a necrotic / non-enhancing core (confidence 0.54). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The whole-tumour mass is predominantly left-sided (confidence 1.00).
An enhancing tumour component is present (confidence 0.90).
Whole-tumour burden is assessed as small (volume tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.56). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The enhancing fraction of the whole tumour is high (ET/WT tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.75).
Acquisition quality (cjv, efc, snr, sharpness, inu, contrast, entropy) is mildly outside the training cohort range (mean |z| = 0.81); interpret borderline findings with corresponding caution.
T1 and T1ce show a hyperintense lesion with a central area of low signal intensity, consistent with a lesion of low signal intensity on T2 and FLAIR sequences.
The lesion appears to have a mild mass effect on the surrounding brain tissue, but no resection cavity or midline shift is observed.
DEFERRED TO RADIOLOGIST: case confidence 0.54 is below the calibrated gate threshold 0.55.
For radiologist confirmation: ncr_present present (p=0.54); laterality left (p=1.00).
